questions.question: There were two candidates in an election, 10% of voters did not vote and 48 votes were found invalid. The winning candidate got 53% of all the voters in the list and won by 304 votes. Find the total number of votes enrolled.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

There were two candidates in an election, 10% of voters did not vote and 48 votes were found invalid. The winning candidate got 53% of the total votes and won by 304 votes.

**Concept used:**

Percentage

**Calculation:**

Let the total number of voters be 100x

10% of voters did not vote 

Number of voters who vote = 100x - 10x = 90x

48 votes were found invalid

Valid votes = 90x - 48

Votes gained by the winning candidate = frac{{53}}{{100}} times 100x = 53x

Votes gained by the loosing candidate = 90x - 48 - 53x

⇒ 37x - 48

As per the question,

⇒ 53x - (37x - 48) = 304

⇒ 16x = 304 - 48

⇒ 16x = 256

⇒ x = 16

**∴ Total number of voters = 100x = 1600**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__** 

Let total number of votes be 100 units,

10% voters did not cast their vote

⇒ Votes polled = 90 units

The winning candidate got 53% of all the voters in the list and won by 304 votes,

⇒ Winning candidate got = 53 units votes

⇒ Other candidate got = 37 units votes

⇒ Difference in votes = 53 units votes - 37 units votes = 304 - 48 = 256 votes

⇒ 16 units = 256

∴ 100 units votes = 256/16 × 100 = 1600 votes

∴ Total number of voters = 1600.

questions.question: In a class 40% are boys and rest are girls. If 60% of the girls and 40% boys passed in the test, what percent of total students passed?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Number of boys in the class = 40% of the total students

Number of boys passed the test = 40% of boys

Number of girls passed in the test = 60% of girls

**Calculation:**

Let the total number of students in the class be 100.

Number of boys = 40% of 100

⇒ (40/100) × 100 = 40

Number of girls = 100 - 40 = 60

The number of boys passed the test = 40% × 40

⇒ (40/100) × 40 = 16

The number of girls passed the test = 60% × 60

⇒ (60/100) × 60 = 36

Total students passed the test = 16 + 36 = 52

Now, required percentage = (52/100) × 100 = 52%

**∴ The percent of total students passed is 52%.**

questions.question: Some students attended the paper of Hindi or English or both of them in the exam. If 70% of students attended the paper of Hindi, 50% gave paper of English then how many of them attend both papers?
questions.solution:

**Calculations:**

**∴ Students who attend both papers = 100% - 80% = 20%**

questions.question: Suresh gives 25 percent of an amount to his wife, 45 percent to his daughter, and 20 percent of the remaining part to his son. If Suresh is left with Rs. 4800, then how much did Suresh have in the beginning?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Suresh gives 25 percent of an amount to his wife

Suresh gives 45 percent to his daughter and

Suresh gives 20 percent of the remaining part to his son

Amount left at the end is Rs. 4800

**Calculation:**

Let the total initial amount with Suresh be 100.

According to the question,

Suresh gives 25 percent of an amount to his wife

⇒ The amount left now = 100 - 25 = 75.

Then, Suresh gives 45 percent to his daughter

⇒ The amount left now = 75 - 45 = 30

Then Suresh gives 20 percent of the remaining part to his son,

⇒ 20% × 30 = 6

⇒ The amount left now = 30 - 6 = 24

Now 24 ≡ Rs. 4800 ( ≡ is a equivalent symbol)

⇒ So 100 ≡ (4800/24) × 100 

⇒ 100 ≡ 20000

**∴ Suresh had Rs. 20000 in the beginning.**

questions.question: A man spends 75% of his income. If his income increases by 20% and his expenditure also increase by 10%. The percentage of increase in his savings is
questions.solution:
**Given Data:**

Spends 75% of his income

Income increases by 20%

Expenditure increases by 10%

**Calculation:**

Let the income be Rs 100

Expenditure = 75% of 100 = 75

Savings will be = 100 – 75 = 25

Income after the increase by 20% = 120

Expenditure after the increase by 10% = 110% of 75 = 82.5

New savings = New income – New expenditure = 120 – 82.5 = 37.5

Increase in saving = 37.5 – 25 = 12.5

Percent increase in savings = (12.5/25)×100

**∴ Percent increase in savings is 50%**

questions.question: In an examination A got 38% marks and failed by 42 marks. While B got 25% more marks than A and passed by 15 marks. What is the passing percentage for the examination ?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

In an examination A got 38% marks and failed by 42 marks. While B got 25% more marks than A and passed by 15 marks. 

**Concept used:**

Percentage

**Calculation:**

Let the maximum marks for the examination be a.

Marks scored by A

⇒ frac{{38}}{{100}} × a = frac{{19a}}{{50}}

Marks scored by B

⇒ frac{{19a}}{{50}} × frac{{125}}{{100}} = frac{{95a}}{{200}}

As per the question, 

⇒ frac{{19a}}{{50}} + 42 = frac{{95a}}{{200}} - 15 {Keeping the passing marks same.}

⇒ frac{{95a}}{{200}} - frac{{19a}}{{50}} = 57

⇒ frac{{19a}}{{200}} = 57

⇒ a = 3 × 200 = 600

Passing marks = ( {600 times frac{{19}}{{50}}} ) + 42 = 270

∴ Required passing percentage = frac{{270}}{{600}} times 100 = 45\%

questions.question: In an examination, C got 25% less marks than B and A got 20% more marks than C. Find the marks which B got if difference between A’s marks and B’s marks is 36.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

C got 25% less marks than B

A got 20% more marks than C

Difference between B’s marks and A’s marks = 36

**Calculation:**

Let marks obtained by B be x

Then, marks obtained by C = x × (100 – 25)/100

⇒ 0.75x

And, marks obtained by A = 0.75x × (100 + 20)/100

⇒ 0.9x

Now, A/c to question

⇒ x – 0.9x = 36

⇒ 0.1x = 36

⇒ x = 360

**∴ ****B got 360 marks**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Let B got 100% marks

⇒ C got = 75% marks

⇒ A got = 90% marks (120/100 × 75 = 90%)

Now, 100% – 90% = 36

⇒ 10% = 36

⇒ 100% = 360

**∴ ****B got 360 marks**
